To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the plasma membrane contains a large number of glycoproteins, the structure and function of which can be modulated by changes of the carbohydrate side chains, and that these changes may be involved in the regulation of cellular response to trophotropic stimuli.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of plasma membranes in the regulation of cellular response to trophics stimuli.
the role of membrane glycoprotein structure in mediating cellular response to trophics stimuli.
the role of glycoproteins and glycolipids in the mediation of trophic effects of growth factors, in particular the epidermal growth factor (EGF) and its receptors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
membrane glycoprote-ins play a central role in the integration of cellular functions, in particular of cellular response to extracellular signals.
the plasma membrane glycoprotein is a multifunctional macromolecule with a complex structure and a complex mode of biosynthesis and degradation.
the oligosaccha-ride moieties of glycoproteins are involved in the regulation of cellular response to trophics stimuli.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the plasma membrane is the most complex membrane in the cell.
membrane glycoproteines are important for the regulation of cell growth and differentiation.
membrane glycoprotei ns are important mediators of cell-cell and cell matrix recognition, and that their synthesis and degradation are under the control of trophic stimuli.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the oligosac-charide side chains of membrane glycoprotein play an essential role in the regulation of the cell surface function.
the plasma membrane glycoprotein is a complex and dynamic structure, which is continuously remodeled during growth and differentiation.

the glycoprotein structure of the cell surface is dynamic and is subject to change during the course of cell growth and differentiation, and that the glycoproteins of the plasma membrane may play an important role in the regulation of cellular responses to trophic stimulation.
